<STATEMENT>
# Problem A — Backbone Trenching for the Control Vault

Time limit: 5 s   Memory limit: 256 MB

## Description
A new control vault is being commissioned, and its modules must be installed along a single straight
equipment trench. The trench is divided into a fixed number of consecutive mounting bays, exactly one
module per bay, and every module ends up in some bay; there are precisely as many bays as modules, so the
installation is a one-to-one placement of modules onto bay positions numbered along the trench.

The modules exchange signals over point-to-point harnesses. Whenever two modules must exchange signals, a
harness is run between their bays through the trench's cable tray. Because the tray runs the length of the
trench, the physical length of a harness is determined solely by how many bay positions separate the two
modules it connects — adjacent bays cost one unit of harness, bays two apart cost two units, and so on.
By the physical geometry of the trench, the length contributed by any single harness is always an integer, and no single harness can ever equal or exceed $n$ units in length.
The specific routing hardware, connector types, and signal directions are immaterial to this calculation;
only the separation in bays matters.

Procurement has fixed a **total** harness budget for the job: summed over every required signal harness,
the combined harness length must not exceed the given budget. There is no per-harness limit and no limit
on how many harnesses share the tray — the only constraint that binds is the grand total.

Decide whether the modules can be placed one-per-bay so that the total harness length over all required
connections stays within the budget, and if so output a placement; otherwise report that no placement
fits the budget. (A placement that is excellent for some connections may overshoot the total because of
others, so local good choices do not guarantee a feasible total.)

## Input
First line: three integers $n$, $m$, $B$. 
Each of the next $m$ lines: two integers $u$ $v$ — representing a harness between module $u$ and module $v$.

## Output
Print `YES` then a line with $n$ integers — the position (1 to $n$, forming a permutation) of module 1, 2, ..., $n$ —
such that the total harness length is $\le B$. Otherwise print `NO`.

## Example 1

### Input
```
4 4 6
1 2
2 3
3 4
4 1
```

### Output
```
YES
1 2 4 3
```

## Example 2

### Input
```
4 4 5
1 2
2 3
3 4
4 1
```

### Output
```
NO
```
</STATEMENT>
